llm.summary: This skill is a scoped helper for comparing public app privacy disclosures through Crawlora, with the outbound API use and API key requirement disclosed.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires outbound requests to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 and a CRAWLORA_API_KEY, which is proportionate for a Crawlora-backed comparison workflow and is disclosed in the skill instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time mutation, package installation, service registration, or dependency fetching was found; the bundled shell helper uses curl when invoked by the user or agent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are bounded to documented Crawlora routes, call budgeting, source attribution, and limitations on what privacy disclosures prove; the helper script further restricts use to GET requests and an allowlist of relevant routes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, account modification, credential harvesting, or broad local file access was found; the script stores the API key only in a temporary curl config with restrictive permissions and removes it on exit.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities match its stated purpose: it searches app store listings and retrieves App Store privacy cards, Google Play data-safety disclosures, and Google Play permissions for user-selected apps.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using Crawlora as a third-party service for app-store disclosure lookups. Set a Crawlora API key with the least privilege available, avoid sending unrelated user or device data as query terms, and treat the results as public disclosure comparisons rather than proof of actual app runtime behavior.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill references a bundled shell helper, but the helper is narrow: fixed Crawlora base URL, GET-only behavior, and an allowlist of app privacy routes. This is a packaging/governance note rather than evidence of unsafe behavior.
[E1] expected: External transmission to Crawlora is central to the stated workflow and is disclosed in both SKILL.md and the endpoint reference. The inspected script sends the Crawlora API key only to the fixed Crawlora API host.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 operation does not request sudo or root privileges; it restricts permissions on a temporary curl config file that holds the API key, which is a protective measure.
[SQP-2] expected: The endpoint reference explicitly states the API base and x-api-key header requirement. A clearer credential-handling warning would be useful, but the behavior is not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
